name: Fighter Outback Warrior
body:
To survive poisonous snakes, disease-carrying stinging insects, and deadly apex predators of the jungle, outback warriors must be quick-witted, industrious, and conditioned to achieve the highest level of physical fitness and endurance.

An outback warrior has the following class features.

Class Skills

An outback warrior adds Acrobatics, Knowledge (nature), Perception, and Stealth to their list of class skills, but they do not get Knowledge (dungeoneering) or Knowledge (engineering). Additionally, outback warriors receive 4 + Int modifier skill points per level.

This alters class skills.

Conditioned Defense (Ex)

Outback warriors are proficient with shields (except tower shields), but not with any armor. At 1st level, When not wearing armor and not encumbered, an outback warrior adds their Constitution bonus (if any) to their AC. Additionally, an Outback warrior gains a +1 bonus to AC at 3rd level. This bonus increases by 1 for every 3 outback warrior levels thereafter up to a maximum of +6 at 18th level. If the outback warrior multiclasses with another class that adds an ability modifier to AC while unarmored (like the monk or shifter’s Wisdom modifier), the outback warrior can choose to add either one of the two ability modifiers from their various classes, but not both.

This alters armor proficiency.

Arboreal Locomotion (Ex)

At 1st level, an outback warrior gains a 20 foot climb speed (gaining a +8 racial bonus to Climb checks) and can move through the upper canopies of jungles and forests without touching the ground by leaping and swinging from branch to branch and tree to tree. No check is necessary to move in this way as long as the outback warrior has both hands free and is in a forest (cold, temperate, or warm) terrain.

This replaces the 1st level bonus feat.

Toxicity Resistance (Ex)

At 2nd level, an outback warrior gains a +2 bonus on saving throw rolls against poison and disease. This bonus increases to +6 at 6th level. At 10th level, an outback warrior has immunity to poison and disease.

This replaces the bonus feats gained at 2nd, 6th, and 10th level.

Call of the Wild (Sp)

At 3rd level, as a move action, an outback warrior can voice a resounding bellow to cast summon nature’s ally II as a spell-like ability. Only animals, elementals, plants, and vermin can be summoned using this ability. At 7th level, this ability functions as summon nature’s ally IV; at 11th level it functions as summon nature’s ally VI; and at 15th level it functions as summon nature’s ally VIII.

This ability can be used once per day at 3rd level, twice per day at 7th level, and three times per day at 11th level. At 15th level, an outback warrior can activate this ability as a swift action instead of a move action.

This replaces armor training and all of its iterations.

Improved Conditioned Defense (Ex)

At 19th level, an outback warrior gains damage reduction 5/- and is treated as though under the constant effects of endure elements.

This replaces armor mastery.
